headline.en: Haul Away, Joe: hear the whole song first, then the tune on its own.

detail.en: The whole song, every part together
The guide sings it, line by line
Stop if anything tightens or hurts

headline.en: Now the tune on its own.

detail.en: Follow the words as it plays

text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
This is the tune John Short, an old sailor from the harbour town of Watchet, sang for English Folk-Chanteys, printed in 1914.

source.en: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (1914), No. XXVII and its note, read from the scan

text.en: Hear line 1, then sing it back.
Hear line 2, then sing it back.
Now lines 1 and 2 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 3, then sing it back.
Line 4 is line 2 again. Sing it with the guide.
Line 5 is the tune of line 3 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Line 6 is line 2 again. Sing it with the guide.
Now lines 3 to 6 joined, with the guide.
Line 7 is the tune of line 3 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Line 8 is line 2 again. Sing it with the guide.
Hear line 9, then sing it back.
Hear line 10, then sing it back.
Now lines 7 to 10 joined, with the guide.
Chorus start to end, with the guide.
Verse 1 start to end, with the guide.
Verse 2 start to end, with the guide.
Verse 3 start to end, with the guide.
The whole song, with the guide.
Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
Once more on your own, from the top.
Record the tune of Haul Away, Joe in Sing, with the other parts playing.
Other books print this shanty in a major key; Sharp notes that John Short's tune is in the dorian mode, which gives it its darker, older sound.

source.en: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (1914), No. XXVII and its note, read from the scan
